text:
maya: Heads up — nightly embedding+rerank run shows an intermittent MRR drop (~1.7%) for rdl-open-3q quantized builds. Seen this 3/10 runs. Looks like ordering drift rather than model quality. Logs hint at runner batch-affinity churn. Anyone seen this?

liu: Which job / command? seed?

maya: job: ci-eval-5567, ran with:```
./eval_runner --suite embed_rerank --model rdl-open-3q --quant 4bit --seed=42 --workers=8
```
Happened on seeds 42, 97, 204. baseline float32 runs are stable.

ci-bot: CI job ci-eval-5567: https://ci.internal/redwood/jobs/5567 (artifacts + logs attached) :eyes:

sam: Hmm. Batch-affinity scheduling can cause different micro-batching across queries which can change KV-cache timing and evictions. We changed default affinity last week (perf tweak). Could be the cause. Try forcing affinity off: `--batch-affinity=disabled` or `--batch-affinity=stable`.

kevin: I just opened infra PR #412 to set eval clusters' default to `stable-affinity` while we triage. rolling to staging now.

eva: Tried quick local repro with quant=4 seed=42 and `--batch-affinity=disabled` — couldn't repro the MRR drop, but saw these in the logs when it did fail earlier:```
[2026-07-15T03:12:02Z] kvcache: evict prefix convo-123 (reason=batch_eviction)
[2026-07-15T03:12:02Z] runner: assigned batch 17 -> worker 3
[2026-07-15T03:12:02Z] rerank: scores [0.421, 0.421, 0.420]
```
Note the two equal-ish scores then ordering changed across runs.

ryan: Also check the rerank harness tie-breaker — if we rely on nondet map order for equal scores, small reorderings change MRR. We added float rounding last month but maybe not everywhere.

sam: Good catch. There's a known nondet in threadpool map ordering in runner v2.1.3 — we didn't stable-sort candidate ids before final tie-break. I'll push a tiny patch to deterministic-sort before scoring and kick CI.

maya: Please add a test in the eval harness that asserts stable ordering across repeated runs for the same seed+quant config. If we see >0.5% MRR variance across 3 trials mark as flaky.

kevin: Keeping `stable-affinity` default for eval clusters until we have a green signal from deterministic-sort + tests. PR #412 -> merged to staging.

eva: Quick run results (10 seeds, quant=4): 8/10 matched baseline, 2/10 showed earlier drift pattern. After applying deterministic sort locally, those two now match. I'll run larger job tonight.

sam: CI job ci-eval-5599 launched with patch (deterministic sort + affinity stable): https://ci.internal/redwood/jobs/5599 — ping if it flakes.

liu: If deterministic sort fixes ordering variance, still want to recorded why quantized runs are more sensitive. Could be numeric tie frequency increases with quantization. Add a small unit test that forces many equal scores to stress tie-breaking.

maya: Agreed. Action items: 1) sam add patch + unit test, 2) liu add tie-breaker stress test to harness, 3) kevin keep stable-affinity for eval infra, 4) eva run larger seed sweep and share artifacts.

ryan: If this stops flaking, let's also add a dashboard alert: rerank MRR variance >0.5% across last 5 runs => investigation ticket auto-created.

maya: ack. If it still flakes after deterministic tie-break + stable-affinity we'll dig deeper into quantization nondeterminism (kernel scheduling, fp->int rounding).

sam: I'll post the patch shortly. thx all :thumbsup:

eva: dropping repro script and raw outputs: /tmp/embed-repro/quant-4/ -> uploaded to job artifacts.

maya: Great, thanks. Follow-up tomorrow after the big sweep.
